mainEntity.name: How is a long-distance move priced — and why is there no per-mile rate?

acceptedAnswer.text: You will get a delivery window set for your move from your dates; we publish no standard spread, because the honest width depends on the lane, the load and the season. In wider industry practice, spreads of 7 to 21 days are common on consolidated runs, and the driver calls ahead of arrival (5). Plan around the window — essentials with you, far-end commitments loose — and it stops being a risk.

mainEntity.name: Will I get an exact delivery date?

acceptedAnswer.text: Anything worth more than $100 per pound — FMCSA's examples include jewelry, silverware, china, furs, antiques and oriental rugs. List each article specifically, in writing, on the shipping documents before loading: unless you declare it, a mover may limit its liability for that article even under Full Value Protection (1, 3). On our moves the declaration is part of the inventory step.

mainEntity.name: What should I declare as high-value, and how?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes — planned as its own job inside the move. Pieces of 1,500 to 3,500 lbs move under SIR and, for safes, the KIM-GS Protocol: survey, L/360 floor check, load spreading and verified placement at both ends (5, 6). A safe is emptied by you before it moves, always; contents are never discussed or handled. Our Winchester to Las Vegas pages show the pattern end to end (6).

mainEntity.name: Can a gun safe or a piano travel with the rest of the household?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Valuation is the mover's own liability level under federal rule — Full Value Protection, where the mover repairs, replaces or pays current replacement value, or Released Value at 60 cents per pound per article if you sign the waiver (1, 3). It is a tariff level of liability, not an insurance policy; third-party insurance is a different purchase entirely (1).

mainEntity.name: Is valuation the same as insurance?

mainEntity.name: When should I book a long-distance move?
How long do I have to file a claim — and how fast must the mover answer?

acceptedAnswer.text: Nine months from the date of delivery, in writing. The mover must acknowledge your claim within 30 days and pay it, deny it, or make a settlement offer within 120 days. If it is denied, the mover must offer neutral arbitration, or you can sue under 49 U.S.C. 14706. Note anything missing or damaged on the delivery receipt before you sign — that notation is the evidence the claim stands on.

mainEntity.name: What is the 110% rule at delivery?

acceptedAnswer.text: It belongs to non-binding estimates: at delivery, a mover cannot require more than the estimate plus 10 percent, and you get at least 30 days after delivery to pay the balance. Our price works differently — reviewed in full and agreed as one flat rate in writing before the truck rolls. Either way, know which kind of document you are holding before you sign it.

mainEntity.name: What does "reasonable dispatch" mean for my delivery?

acceptedAnswer.text: It is the federal performance standard: the mover must perform on the dates, or inside the delivery spread, written on the order for service and bill of lading. If the spread is missed, lodging and food for the days past it can be claimed with receipts, within nine months of delivery.

mainEntity.name: How is a grand piano prepared for a long-distance move — and when do I tune it?

acceptedAnswer.text: Legs and pedal lyre come off and are packed separately; the case is lowered onto a padded piano board on its straight side and strapped to the vehicle structure, nothing loaded on top. After delivery, wait 10 to 14 days before tuning — a month or more after a big climate change — so the instrument equalizes to the new room first.

mainEntity.name: How is fine art packed for a long haul?

acceptedAnswer.text: Photographs and a signed condition report first. Glassine or acid-free tissue is the first layer against an unglazed surface — never bubble wrap or cling film on the surface itself. Paintings travel vertical, never flat, and high-value pieces ride in bespoke crates with foam cavities that float them against shock, in the 45 to 55 percent relative humidity band conservation guidance sets for transport.

mainEntity.name: What if my new home is not ready when the truck arrives?

acceptedAnswer.text: Your goods can wait in our storage — leased space that takes household goods and high-value pieces alike, 30-day minimum, and you can access your items while they are stored. It is arranged as part of the move plan before the truck rolls, so a slipped closing date becomes a scheduling detail, not a crisis at the curb.
